# October Drift & Adaptation Investigation (`42_october_drift.py`)

## Executive Summary

**Direct Answer:** There is **no new fraud pattern, changed numeric constant, slower/split bot burst, or new account role in October (`test`)** that is absent or rare in July–September (`train`). Instead, four structural facts explain all October differences and the public leaderboard behavior:

1. **Global 0.50x Exposure Scaling in October (`~8,406 rows/day` vs `~17,000 rows/day` in Jul–Sep):**
   - Monthly row counts are **Jul: `527,065`**, **Aug: `526,852`**, **Sep: `509,996`** (plus `147` Oct-dated train boundary rows = `510,143`), and **Oct (`test`): `260,582`** (`260,536` in `2026-10` plus `46` Nov-1 chain/drain tails) across the **same pool of 420,000 customer accounts and 30,000 merchants**.
   - Because the background arrival rate $\lambda$ per account, merchant, and device in October is **half (`0.50x`)** that of Jul–Sep, every background count-in-window distribution (`rcv_cnt_2m`, `rcv_cnt_10m`, `rcv_cnt_60m`) and consecutive entity time-gap distribution (`snd:dt_prev`, `dev:dt_prev` in `10m–24h`) shifts downward by Poisson scaling ($\text{Poisson}(\lambda)$ vs $\text{Poisson}(2\lambda)$).
2. **Zero New Ratio Recipes in October (Question 1):**
   - Across **33 ratio series** (`balance_before/amount`, `2h` and `24h` prev/next balance and amount ratios per `sender_id`, `receiver_id`, and `device_id`, and `2h`/`24h` outgoing-to-incoming ratios), we tested **29,450 bins** at `0.01` resolution (`round(2)`, total count $\ge 25$) and **77,185 bins** at `0.001` resolution (`round(3)`, total count $\ge 25$).
   - Only **3 bins** at `round(2)` and **7 bins** at `round(3)` had an October rate $>3\times$ the Jul–Sep maximum with $\ge 5$ October rows, and their maximum October count was **12 rows** (vs 3–8 in Jul–Sep)—exact Poisson tail noise across $10^5$ comparisons.
   - Every known numeric constant (`0.25x` SIM-swap drain, `0.35x` ATO drain, `1.10x` phishing/cashback payback, `99.0x` under-1000 P2P collect, `1.02x` mule forward, `0.90–1.00x` layering hop, and `{1000, 2000, 2500, 5000, 10000}` merchant `S_flag`) occurs at the **exact same constant** in October.
3. **Only Two Known Signatures Dropped in Per-Row Rate in October—and Neither Mutated Into a New Shape (Question 2):**
   - **`velocity_bot` (`bot_Qs_ge3`)** fell from **`247.98 / 183.73 / 209.02` per 100k** (`33 / 26 / 25` bursts) in Jul/Aug/Sep to **`103.23` per 100k** (`269` rows across `7` bursts of size 25–60) in October (**`0.483x`** of the Jul–Sep mean, **`0.494x`** of Sep). In the shared bot device pool (`DV0420001–DV0423000`), October has `269` total rows on `7` devices and **all `269` (100%) are inside `Qs_n >= 3` (`0` residual rows)**. In the test band-2 block (`DV0473750–DV0473825`), there are `22` rows (`1` in a mule fan-in, `2` in a drain burst, and `19` isolated ordinary-looking singletons—matching the train band-2 singleton density). Relaxing amount ceiling, fractional amounts, window length up to 24h, multi-device merchant bursts, P2P bursts, or other `txn_type` finds **zero** replacement bot bursts.
   - **`merchant_collusion` (`S_flag == 1 & S_n >= 10`)** fell from **`48.21 / 49.22` per 100k** in Aug/Sep (`14` sessions each) to **`27.25` per 100k** in October (`71` rows in `3` sessions of sizes 21, 24, 26; **`0.554x`** of Sep, though equal to July's **`25.80` per 100k**). Total `S_flag` rate did **not** fall (`110.99 / 138.37 / 131.37 / 127.41` per 100k); in October `S_n in 1..3` (`qr_swap`) is `70.99/100k` and `S_n in 4..8` (`refund_abuse`) is `29.17/100k`. Widening the session time gap from `1 day` to `2, 3, or 7 days` does not merge smaller sessions into `S_n >= 10` (`71` rows for 1d/2d/3d, `82` rows at 7d).
   - **Why public per-group scores were weaker on `SIM-swap+takeover` and `QR+refund+collusion` despite constant recipe rates:** Each fraud class in both train and test is a mixture of **~55% patterned recipe events** and **~45% featureless ordinary-looking fraud rows** (drawn from the background distribution, where only ~16% sit on fraud-band devices). In train (`Jul–Sep`), patterned fraud carried two strong generator traps (`app_major == '3'` at 62% vs 15% legit, and `ip_risk_score > 0.5` at 40% vs 2% legit), which vanished in October (`app_version` 5.0/5.1/5.2 uniform; `ip_risk_score > 0.5` down to 1.0–1.3%).
4. **Two Recipe Boundary Refinements Discovered via Band-Device Forensics (Present Equally in Jul–Sep and Oct, Questions 2 & 3):**
   - **Mule victim fan-ins where `new_payee == 0` on most victim rows:** `features_v1`/`v2` required `new_payee == 1` inside `vict = pay & is_p2p & newp & a_int & (amt % 10 == 0)`. Dropping `new_payee == 1` at `rcv_cnt_24h >= 5` recovers **`+82 / +103 / +136 / +59` rows** (`15.56 / 19.55 / 26.67 / 22.64` per 100k in Jul/Aug/Sep/Oct; `85%` raw `mule_account` in train with `app_major == '3'` share `0.620`), including test band-1 rows `TX80e376fa` and `TXde88f2ce`.
   - **Layering chains with hop gaps between `2 h` and `6 h`:** `features_v5.py` capped hop gaps at `W = 7200s` (2h). Widening `W` to `21,600s` (6h) for `ch_len >= 3` recovers **`+123 / +123 / +111 / +77` rows** (`23.34 / 23.35 / 21.76 / 29.55` per 100k in Jul/Aug/Sep/Oct; `app_major == '3'` share `0.630` in train), turning the apparent slight dip in `ch_len >= 3` (`129.0 / 140.6 / 132.2 -> 120.9/100k`) into a completely flat rate (**`161.8 / 177.3 / 164.9 -> 164.6/100k`**) and recovering test band-3 rows `TX1ddc6121` and `TX6eb03351`.

#### Exact Integer Burst Sizes (`k >= 2`, `tot >= 15`) with $>3\times$ Drift in Centered (`_pm`) Windows
- **Upward exact burst sizes (`Oct_r > 3x max(Jul-Sep)` and `Oct >= 5`):** Only **2 exact burst events** appear across all 9 centered window series:
  1. `dev_cnt_10m_pm == 29`: Jul `17` (`3.23/100k`), Aug `2` (`0.38`), Sep `0` (`0.00`), Oct **`30` (`11.51/100k`, `3.57x`)** — a single 29-row `velocity_bot` burst on one device.
  2. `rcv_cnt_10m_pm == 58` (and `rcv_cnt_2m_pm` in `42, 45, 46, 47, 48`): Jul `0`, Aug `0`, Sep `0`, Oct **`58` (`22.26/100k`)** — a single 58-row `velocity_bot` burst targeting one merchant.
- **Downward exact burst sizes (`Oct_r < 1/3x min(Jul-Sep)`):**
  - In `dev_cnt_10m_pm`: exact integer sizes `30, 34, 37, 42, 46, 48, 49, 53, 55, 57, 58` happen to have `0` bursts in October because October has only `7` total bot bursts (sizes `26, 29, 32, 35, 41, 48-split, 58`) vs `25–33` bursts per month in Jul–Sep.
  - In `rcv_cnt_2m_pm` (`k = 7..13`), `rcv_cnt_10m_pm` (`k = 24..41`), and `rcv_cnt_60m_pm` (`k = 108..226`): high background merchant arrival counts drop to `0` in October because busy merchants receive ~`55` txns/hour in October instead of ~`110` txns/hour in Jul–Sep ($0.50\times$ global exposure scaling).

### 2.2 Detailed Search for Where Missing Events Went
#### A. `velocity_bot` (`bot_Qs_ge3`: `247.98 / 183.73 / 209.02` $\rightarrow$ `103.23` per 100k, `-51.7%` vs Jul–Sep)
We tested five hypotheses for where the missing October bot bursts might have gone:
1. **Same shared bot device pool (`DV0420001–DV0423000`) with a different constant, amount range, or slower pace:**
   - Total rows on `DV0420001–DV0423000`: Jul `1,307` (on `33` devices), Aug `969` (on `27` devices), Sep `1,066` (on `25` devices), Oct **`269` (on `7` devices)**.
   - Rows on `DV0420001–DV0423000` NOT matching `Qs_n >= 3`: Jul **`0`**, Aug **`1`**, Sep **`0`**, Oct **`0`**.
   - Every active bot-pool device in October produces a textbook 25–60 row whole-rupee merchant burst in 5–10 minutes; the remaining 2,993 devices in `DV0420001–DV0423000` have **zero** transactions in October.
2. **Test Band-2 device block (`DV0473750–DV0473825`, 76 devices):**
   - Contains **`22` rows across `22` distinct devices** (`1` row per device; `0` devices with $\ge 2$ rows in October).
   - Of those `22` rows: `1` is in a mule victim fan-in (`TXc6b77f80`), `2` are inside `0.25x`/`0.35x` drain bursts (`TX530faaf2`, `TX209739fc`), and `19` are isolated ordinary-looking singletons—matching the exact ordinary-fraud singleton rate in train's Band-2 block (`129` singletons across 3 months vs `19` in half-sized October).
3. **Relaxing amount ceiling (`amount <= 500`, `<= 5000`, or any amount), allowing paise (`amt_is_int == 0`), or changing `txn_type` / `receiver_type` (P2P instead of MERCHANT):**
   - Any device with $\ge 10$ rows in 10 minutes across the entire dataset (any `amount`, any `txn_type`, `P2P` or `MERCHANT`): Jul `1,307`, Aug `968`, Sep `1,066`, Oct **`269`** (**0 extra rows** beyond standard `bot_Qs_ge3`).
4. **Slower or split bursts on one device (`5..24` rows in `10m`, `60m`, or `24h`):**
   - Any device with $\ge 15$ rows in `60m` or `24h` (any amount/type): Jul `1,307`, Aug `968`, Sep `1,066`, Oct **`269`** (**0 extra rows**).
   - Devices with `5..14` integer merchant payments in `60m` (outside `Qs_n >= 15` and `S_flag`): Jul `6` rows, Aug `0` rows, Sep `0` rows, Oct **`0` rows**.
5. **Multi-device bursts targeting a single merchant (`receiver_id` with $\ge 15$ small integer payments in `10m` across multiple devices):**
   - Outside the `269` known single-device bot rows, no merchant in October has a burst of small integer payments across multiple devices.
   - **Conclusion on `velocity_bot`:** The generator simply sampled `7` bot burst events in October (`103.23/100k`) instead of the `12–16` events expected at constant per-row rate.

#### B. `merchant_collusion` (`S_flag == 1 & S_n >= 10`: `25.80 / 48.21 / 49.22` $\rightarrow$ `27.25` per 100k)
1. **Total `S_flag` (`MERCHANT` `PAY`/`QR` with `amount in {1000, 2000, 2500, 5000, 10000}`) is completely unchanged in October:**
   - Total `S_flag` rate: Jul `110.99/100k` (`585`), Aug `138.37/100k` (`729`), Sep `131.37/100k` (`670`), Oct **`127.41/100k` (`332`, `1.004x` of Jul–Sep mean)**.
   - Breakdown by session size `S_n` (`gap <= 1 day`):
     - `S_n in 1..3` (`qr_swap` branch): `62.23 / 63.21 / 60.98` $\rightarrow$ **`70.99/100k`** (`185` rows in Oct, `1.14x`).
     - `S_n in 4..8` (`refund_abuse` branch): `22.96 / 26.95 / 21.18` $\rightarrow$ **`29.17/100k`** (`76` rows in Oct, `1.23x`).
     - `S_n >= 10` (`merchant_collusion` branch): `25.80 / 48.21 / 49.22` $\rightarrow$ **`27.25/100k`** (`71` rows in Oct across `3` sessions of sizes `21, 24, 26`—matching July's `25.80/100k`).
2. **Testing whether slower/split sessions (`gap <= 2d, 3d, 7d`) or other round constants (`% 500 == 0`, `% 100 == 0`) hide split collusion sessions:**
   - Widening the session gap from `1d` to `2d` or `3d` leaves `S_n >= 10` in October at **`71` rows** (`0` split sessions merged); widening to `7d` merges only one 11-row merchant group (`82` rows, `31.5/100k`, vs `27.9/100k` in Jul).
   - Merchant `bal = 1.1 * amount` (`cashback_abuse` branch) is **`64.09/100k`** in October vs `51.04 / 69.66 / 61.96` in Jul/Aug/Sep (`1.05x`).

#### C. Drain `amount == 500` Floor (`drain_eq500_in_Ds`: `83.29 / 68.33 / 69.22` $\rightarrow$ `55.26` per 100k)
- While `drain_eq500_in_Ds` dipped slightly in October (`55.26/100k`), the **parent drain signature (`drain_Ds_ge2`, `drain_x025_snd`, `drain_x035_snd`) did NOT fall**:
  - `drain_x025_snd`: `120.10 / 111.99 / 105.69` $\rightarrow$ **`109.75/100k`** (`102` bursts in Oct vs `191–223` in Jul–Sep; `Oct/Sep = 1.038x`).
  - `drain_x035_snd`: `125.41 / 104.77 / 104.71` $\rightarrow$ **`110.91/100k`** (`103` bursts in Oct vs `185–227` in Jul–Sep; `Oct/Sep = 1.059x`).
  - Inside `Ds_n >= 2`, `97.2%` of consecutive sender balance ratios in October (`351 / 361`) are exact `0.25` (`166`) or `0.35` (`185`), identical to Jul–Sep (`95.4%`). The slight dip in `amount == 500` rows occurs only because random starting balances in October hit the ₹500 floor slightly fewer times at the tail of the same 2–5 step drain bursts.

### 3.2 What the Unmatched Band-Device Rows Have in Common (`Test` vs. `Train` Comparison)
Comparing the **`217` unmatched test band-device rows** against the **`1182` unmatched train band-device rows** reveals that they are **structurally identical across both splits**:
1. **100% are device singletons (`c_dev_3d == 1`):**
   - **Test unmatched:** `217 / 217` (`100.0%`) have zero other rows on the same `device_id` within $\pm 3$ days (and across the entire month).
   - **Train unmatched:** `1182 / 1182` (`100.0%`) have zero other rows on the same `device_id` within $\pm 3$ days.
2. **100% are non-home, newly allocated devices (`home_device == 0`, `device_age_days < 45`):**
   - **Test unmatched:** `home_device == 0` on `100.0%`, `device_age_days` mean `13.75d` (max `29.80d`).
   - **Train unmatched:** `home_device == 0` on `99.9%` (`1182/1182`), `device_age_days` mean `14.96d`.
3. **Only 6 test rows (`2.8%`) and 35 train rows (`3.0%`) sit on the boundary of a patterned recipe:**
   - **Band 1 (`mule_account`):** `2` test rows (`TX80e376fa`, `TXde88f2ce`) and `6` train rows are integer multiple-of-10 P2P PAY rows into a high-fan-in mule receiver (`rcv_cnt_24h >= 5`) where `new_payee == 0`.
   - **Band 3 (`layering_chain`):** `2` test rows (`TX1ddc6121`, `TX6eb03351`) and `11` train rows are hops of a 3–5 step P2P layering chain (`ratio in [0.90, 1.00]`) whose inter-hop time gap is between `2h` and `6h` (`111m–310m`).
   - **Band 8 (`phishing_collect`) / Band 10 (`cashback_abuse`):** `2` test rows (`TX26c902e1` integer P2P COLLECT with `new_payee=1`; `TX8e270b92` isolated `amount=2` P2P PAY bait) and `18` train rows are isolated baits or integer P2P COLLECTs without a paired `1.10x` payback.
4. **The remaining `212` test rows (`97.7%`) and `1161` train rows (`98.2%`) are pure 'ordinary-looking fraud' draws from the background distribution:**
   - **In Train (`n = 1182`):** Their generator trap shares are **`app_major == '3'`: `16.9%`** (vs **`61.7%`** on matched train band rows and **`15.0%`** on legit rows) and **`ip_risk_score > 0.5`: `3.5%`** (vs **`40.2%`** on matched train band rows and **`2.0%`** on legit rows).
   - **Fractional paise amounts:** `66.8%` of test unmatched rows and `71.8%` of train unmatched rows have fractional amounts (vs `~70%` on legit background rows).
   - **Transaction types (`PAY / QR / COLLECT / AUTOPAY / REFUND`):** Test unmatched is `56.2% / 38.7% / 2.8% / 1.8% / 0.5%`, matching Train unmatched (`58.8% / 34.1% / 3.4% / 3.5% / 0.3%`) and ordinary background traffic.
   - **No hidden multi-row link within $\pm 3$ days:** Aside from the 6 test / 35 train boundary rows above, `71.4%` of test unmatched rows (`57.5%` in higher-density train) have **zero** other rows on the same `sender_id` within $\pm 3$ days, and when sender or receiver neighbors exist within $\pm 3$ days, they are ordinary background transactions on the account's regular `home_device == 1`.

### 4.2 Key Takeaways on the Six Columns in October
1. **`app_version` (`5.0 / 5.1 / 5.2` in October):** Completely uniform (`~33.3%` each) across band-device rows (`33.13% / 32.41% / 34.45%`), non-band known-signature rows (`33.53% / 32.38% / 34.09%`), and all other test rows (`33.46% / 33.44% / 33.10%`). Unlike train's `app_major == '3'` trap, October `app_version` carries **zero** signal ($\chi^2 = 1.62$, $p = 0.80$ across 6 group-by-version cells).
2. **`ip_risk_score`:** In train, patterned fraud had mean `0.42` and `40.4%` with `ip_risk_score > 0.5` (vs `2.0%` on legit). In October, that high-risk tail was largely turned off (`ip_risk_score > 0.5` is only `1.08%` on band-device rows and `1.56%` on non-band known-signature rows vs `0.65%` on other test rows), leaving only a tiny residual mean shift (`0.231` and `0.235` vs `0.220`).
3. **`device_age_days`:** Strongly separates **band-device rows** (`mean = 15.1d`, `p50 = 10.7d`, `p90 = 39.2d`, `85.1% < 30d`) from both non-band known-signature rows (`mean = 324.3d`, `p50 = 260.2d`) and other test rows (`mean = 308.2d`, `p50 = 242.0d`), because every fraud-band device is a newly created non-home device (`home_device == 0`), whereas non-band signature rows occur mostly on existing home devices.
4. **`sim_age_hours`:** Shows a left-tail enrichment (`sim_age_hours < 168h` is `14.18%` on the 5 prompt-signature families and `8.73%` across all 11 recipes vs `2.34%` on other test rows), driven specifically by `sim_swap` (`0.25x` drain) bursts where SIM age is freshly reset.
5. **`login_to_txn_sec`:** Lower on band-device rows (`mean = 46.5s`, `p10 = 3s`, `p50 = 26s`, `39.1% <= 10s`) than on non-band signature rows (`mean = 62.9s`, `p50 = 40s`) and other test rows (`mean = 67.0s`, `p50 = 45s`), driven almost entirely by the `269` `velocity_bot` rows (`median = 4s`) on band-2 / bot-pool devices (unmatched band-device rows have `mean = 66.8s`, `p50 = 46s`—identical to background test rows).
6. **`pin_retries`:** Elevated on band-device rows (`mean = 0.313`, `24.1% >= 1`) vs non-band signature rows (`mean = 0.122`, `11.1% >= 1`) and other test rows (`mean = 0.120`, `11.0% >= 1`), driven by `velocity_bot`, `sim_swap`, and `account_takeover` bursts on band devices (unmatched band-device rows have `mean = 0.138`, matching background).
